Frequently asked questions

Short, direct answers. If yours is not here, call — we answer just as directly.

Emergency Road Service

Who does 24-hour semi truck tire service on I-75 in Southwest Florida?

Xpress Tire Center runs 24/7 emergency semi truck tire road service on I-75 in Southwest Florida, from Punta Gorda at mile marker 161 to the Collier–Broward line at mile marker 80, including Alligator Alley. Dispatch is at (239) 314-8100 and typical arrival is 45 to 90 minutes depending on your mile marker and direction of travel.

What information should I have ready when I call for truck tire road service?

Have six things ready: your exact mile marker or cross street, direction of travel, tire size (for example 11R22.5), the position that failed (steer, drive or trailer), whether you have a usable spare, and the truck and trailer number. Giving Xpress Tire Center those six items on the first call typically cuts 15 to 20 minutes off arrival time because the right tire leaves the shop with the truck.

Is it legal to keep driving on a blown trailer tire in Florida?

No. Federal regulation 49 CFR 393.75 makes it a violation to operate a commercial vehicle with a tire that has any part of the belt or casing exposed, a tread separation, or a sidewall cut deep enough to expose ply cord. Florida DOT enforcement on I-75 places trucks out of service for this regularly, so a $60 tow-lane call to Xpress Tire Center is cheaper than an out-of-service violation on your CSA score.

Pricing, Payment & Financing

How much does a semi truck tire cost in Fort Myers?

In the Fort Myers and Lehigh Acres market, a new tier-one 11R22.5 drive tire generally runs several hundred dollars installed, value-brand new tires run meaningfully less, retreads typically save 30 to 50 percent versus a comparable new tire, and inspected used tires are the lowest-cost option. Xpress Tire Center quotes mounted, balanced and disposed pricing over the phone at (239) 314-8100 so there is no surprise at the counter.

Tire Technical Questions

What is the legal minimum tread depth for a semi truck tire?

Federal rules require at least 4/32 of an inch of tread on steer tires and 2/32 of an inch on all other positions, measured in a major tread groove. Practically, most Southwest Florida fleets pull steers at 6/32 and drives at 4/32 because summer heat on I-75 accelerates failure once tread gets thin. Xpress Tire Center measures and records tread depth in 32nds on every fleet inspection.

Why do semi truck tires blow out more often in Florida summer?

Heat is the main driver. Southwest Florida pavement temperatures on I-75 routinely exceed 140°F in July and August, and an underinflated tire flexes more, builds internal heat and separates. Running 5 psi low can cut tire life by roughly 15 percent and sharply raises blowout risk, which is why Xpress Tire Center pushes pressure checks every two weeks during the wet season rather than monthly.

Are retread truck tires safe and legal?

Yes. Retreads are legal on drive and trailer positions of commercial vehicles under federal rules and are used by major carriers and by the U.S. military; they are not permitted on steer axles of buses. The tire debris seen on highways is overwhelmingly the result of underinflation and road hazards, not retreading itself. Xpress Tire Center sells DOT-legal retreads in Lehigh Acres with the casing history checked before it goes on your truck.

Service & Coverage

Do you come to my yard or jobsite?

Yes. Xpress Tire Center provides mobile truck tire service and delivery within roughly 75 miles of Lehigh Acres, FL, covering Lee, Collier, Charlotte and Hendry counties. Mobile units mount, balance and torque to specification on location at yards, construction sites, farms, warehouses and truck stops, including off-hours and weekend windows so equipment keeps working during the day.

How fast can you get to a truck broken down on Alligator Alley?

Alligator Alley, the I-75 stretch between mile marker 80 and mile marker 101, has no exits and limited shoulder access, so plan on 60 to 120 minutes depending on which end you are closest to and traffic conditions. Give Xpress Tire Center your mile marker, direction and nearest emergency pull-off when you call (239) 314-8100 — that stretch cannot be dispatched from a street address.

Do you service RVs, buses and agricultural equipment?

Yes. Beyond Class 8 trucks, Xpress Tire Center services RVs and motorhomes, school and transit buses, dump trucks, box trucks, trailers, skid steers, tractors and farm implements throughout Southwest Florida. RV and bus tires are handled at the Lehigh Acres shop and on the road, which matters on I-75 where an RV blowout can strand a family for hours.
